svg.title: CausalLab: adding a collider can invalidate a backdoor adjustment set
svg.desc: A fixed DAG and all eight subsets of available A,B,C. The empty set passes the sufficient backdoor criterion; C alone fails by opening a collider; adding A or B repairs it. Separate fixtures require confounder Z, forbid descendant mediator M, and find no set among an available mediator when common cause U is unavailable. No set is not a proof of non-identifiability.

svg.text: CausalLab | more controls can create bias
A supplied causal DAG, a sufficient backdoor criterion, and every subset of explicitly available candidates.
Original supplied graph
A
B
C
X
Y
Conditioning on C opens X <- A -> C <- B -> Y.
For the criterion, remove outgoing X -> Y first.
That graph transformation is not do(X).
Empty adjustment works here; C alone does not.
All available subsets: A, B, C
Adjustment
Backdoor criterion
Minimal?
Inclusion-minimal = no strict valid subset, not fewest controls only.

g.text: Only {} passes; M is a descendant.

svg.text: Valid sets license sum_z P(y | x,z) P(z) only under the causal graph and support assumptions.
The caller declares measurable candidates. Latent common causes must stay in the graph even when unavailable.
No valid backdoor set does not prove non-identifiability. This is not complete adjustment or do-calculus search.
Fixed motifs; full subset audits and graph hashes embedded. No data, empirical effect estimate or graph discovery.
